news.titleTr: GTA 6 ön siparişinde 7,7 milyon barajı aşıldı: Daha çıkmadan 2 milyar dolar gelir!
news.summaryTr: Sensor Tower tahminlerine göre GTA 6, PlayStation ve Xbox platformlarında 7,71 milyon ön sipariş satışına ulaştı. Satışların yüzde 74'ü PlayStation üzerinden gerçekleşirken, oyunun çıkışına kadar 2 milyar dolarlık gelir elde etmesi bekleniyor.
news.articleText: GTA 6 ön siparişinde 7,7 milyon barajı aşıldı: Daha çıkmadan 2 milyar dolar gelir! - Sensor Tower tahminlerine göre GTA 6, PlayStation ve Xbox platformlarında 7,71 milyon ön sipariş satışına ulaştı. Satışların yüzde 74'ü PlayStation üzerinden gerçekleşirken, oyunun çıkışına kadar 2 milyar dolarlık gelir elde etmesi bekleniyor. Sensor Tower verilerine göre konsollardaki toplam brüt gelir 751 milyon dolara ulaştı. Bu tutarın 559 milyon doları PlayStation, 129 milyon doları ise Xbox platformundan elde edildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Böylece PlayStation, hem satış adedinde hem de gelir tarafında Xbox'a önemli ölçüde fark attı. Veriler, oyunun farklı sürümlerine ilişkin ayrıntılı dağılımı ise tam olarak ortaya koymuyor. Ön siparişlerin yüzde 89'u Ultimate Edition Sensor Tower'ın daha önce paylaştığı tahminlere göre ön siparişlerin yüzde 89'u 100 dolarlık Ultimate Edition sürümünden geldi. Sektörde premium sürümlerin toplam satışlar içindeki payının genellikle yüzde 10 ila yüzde 20 arasında değiştiği düşünüldüğünde, bu oran dikkat çekici bir seviyeye işaret ediyor. Çıkış öncesinde 2 milyar dolar gelir beklentisi GTA 6'nın 19 Kasım'daki resmî çıkışına kadar 25 milyon adetlik satışa ulaşabileceği ve yaklaşık 2 milyar dolar gelir yaratabileceği tahmin ediliyor. Bu senaryonun gerçekleşmesi halinde oyunun geliştirme ve pazarlama maliyetlerini çok kısa sürede karşılaması bekleniyor. Ancak söz konusu rakamlar Sensor Tower tahminlerine dayanıyor; kesinleşmiş satış verileri olarak değerlendirilmemeli.

news.summary: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.

news.titleTr: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
news.summaryTr: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.
news.articleText: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck? Tesla CEO Elon Musk has said production of the firm's Cybertruck is "winding down" in Texas, to focus on its self-driving Cybercab cars. The model is only produced at Tesla's Austin base, and he did not clarify if manufacturing would be moved elsewhere or simply cease. The Cybertruck has received a mixed response since its launch in 2023, with some praising its individuality and others simply labelling it ugly. It has also suffered from disappointing sales, quality problems and recalls. BBC's technology reporter Shiona McCallum has this report.

news.title: İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky'a saldırı tehdidi: Güvenlik incelemesi başlatıldı
news.summary: İrlanda kamu yayıncısı RTE'nin de aralarında bulunduğu medya kuruluşlarına yönelik bombalı saldırı tehditlerinin ardından İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky da tehdit aldığını açıkladı. Sky, güvenlik incelemesi başlatıldığını ve ilgili kurumlarla iletişime geçildiğini bildirdi.

news.titleTr: İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky'a saldırı tehdidi: Güvenlik incelemesi başlatıldı
news.summaryTr: İrlanda kamu yayıncısı RTE'nin de aralarında bulunduğu medya kuruluşlarına yönelik bombalı saldırı tehditlerinin ardından İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky da tehdit aldığını açıkladı. Sky, güvenlik incelemesi başlatıldığını ve ilgili kurumlarla iletişime geçildiğini bildirdi.
news.articleText: İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky'a saldırı tehdidi: Güvenlik incelemesi başlatıldı - İrlanda kamu yayıncısı RTE'nin de aralarında bulunduğu medya kuruluşlarına yönelik bombalı saldırı tehditlerinin ardından İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky da tehdit aldığını açıkladı. - Sky, güvenlik incelemesi başlatıldığını ve ilgili kurumlarla iletişime geçildiğini bildirdi. İngiliz yayın kuruluşu Sky, İrlanda'daki medya kuruluşlarını hedef alan bombalı saldırı tehditlerinin ardından kendisinin de güvenlik tehdidi aldığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Sky'dan yapılan açıklamada, "Sky da güvenlik tehdidi alan diğer medya organizasyonlarından biri" ifadeleri kullanıldı. Açıklamada, konuyla ilgili güvenlik incelemesi yapıldığı ve durumun ilgili kurumlara iletildiği belirtildi. Şirket, çalışanlarının ve operasyonlarının güvenliğini sağlamak için yetkili kurumlarla yakın iş birliği içinde çalışıldığını bildirdi. İrlanda'da medya kuruluşları binalarını tahliye etti Bu sabah aralarında İrlanda kamu yayıncısı RTE'nin de bulunduğu bazı medya kuruluşlarına e-posta yoluyla bombalı saldırı tehdidi gönderildi. Tehditlerin ardından kuruluşlar binalarını tahliye ederken canlı yayınlarını da durdurdu. Tehdit alan kuruluşlardan Virgin Media ise binasını boşaltmayarak yayınlarına devam etme kararı aldı. İrlanda Başbakanı Micheal Martin, tehditlerin Avrupa genelinde havacılık sektöründe benzer ihbarlar nedeniyle yaşanan aksaklıkların sürdüğü bir dönemde geldiğine dikkat çekti. Martin, gelişmelerin koordineli bir aksatma kampanyasının parçası olmasının muhtemel göründüğünü ifade etti.

news.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason
news.summary: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason
news.summaryTr: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated.
news.articleText: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason - Published Tanzania's main opposition leader, Tundu Lissu, has been found guilty of inciting unrest and sentenced to four years in jail, in a case that has raised concerns about political freedom in the East African country. A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam acquitted him of the more serious offence of treason, saying prosecutors had failed to prove a key element of that charge. But they said the 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, had encouraged his supporters to disrupt the disputed 2025 general election. Lissu, who leads the opposition Chadema party, has denied the charges, describing the prosecution as politically motivated. The court said his campaign slogan "No Reforms, No Election" was sufficient for him to be convicted of the charge of incitement. "By uttering those words with the intention of disseminating them to the public, the accused incited the public to disrupt the 2025 elections," the court ruled. Lissu said he had only been charged with treason, not incitement. "The offence of incitement is one that you, honourable judges, have manufactured. You have created an offence that did not exist, and you have done so on political directives," Lissu told the court. He added that he would like to apply for bail as this was possible for incitement, unlike treason. He has leave to appeal at the Court of Appeal - the country's highest court. But if the four-year sentence is upheld, it would rule him out of the next elections, due in 2030. Treason is among Tanzania's most serious offences and can carry the death penalty. Human rights group Amnesty International described his conviction as a "travesty of justice". "Tundu Lissu should never have been arrested, let alone prosecuted and convicted," said its regional director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah: President Samia Suluhu Hassan won the October 2025 election with 98% of the vote - a result the opposition dismissed the result as a "mockery" of democracy as her two main challengers, including Lissu, were excluded. Her government has repeatedly denied targeting its opponents. The Chadema leader was arrested six months before the poll, shortly after launching a campaign demanding changes to the electoral system under the slogan "No Reforms, No Election". Prosecutors accused him of making statements intended to incite the public to disrupt the election and threaten the government. They argued that his remarks, which were also circulated online, amounted to treason. But Lissu, a lawyer who represented himself during the trial, maintained that his comments were part of a legitimate political campaign for constitutional and electoral reform. He argued that prosecutors had taken his statements out of context and failed to prove that he had committed any crime. Some of the demands raised by Chadema were: - Electoral commissioners should be independently appointed (not by the president) - Police should allow all parties to campaign free of intimidation - Government-appointed district chiefs should no longer act as returning officers - Party agents should be able to observe counting without harassment - It should be possible to challenge presidential election results in court. During his time in remand custody at Dar es Salaam's Ukonga Prison, Lissu went on hunger strike twice for brief periods when he said he was not allowed access to his lawyers or relatives. He also complained that guards listened to what should have been private consultations his lawyers. These allegations have been denied by the prison authorities. His case has attracted international attention, with rights groups expressing concern about the treatment of opposition politicians and the shrinking space for political dissent in Tanzania. Last year's election was followed by widespread protests and a violent security crackdown that left at least 500 people dead, according to an official inquiry. Opposition groups have said the death toll was much higher and demanded an independent investigation. The government has defended its handling of the unrest and rejected accusations of widespread political repression. Samia, 66, has insisted the election was fair and transparent and blamed foreigners for the unrest, saying it was part of a plot to overthrow her. She has set up another commission to inquiry to identify those behind the violence. Lissu has long been one of Tanzania's most outspoken critics of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party, which, along with its predecessor Tanu, has dominated the country's politics since independence. He first became an MP in 2010, representing a constituency near his birth place in Singida, 320km (200 miles) north-west of the capital, Dodoma. In September 2017, the Chadema politician narrowly survived an assassination attempt when gunmen sprayed his vehicle with bullets outside his home in Dodoma. He was shot multiple times and underwent extensive medical treatment abroad. The attack, whose perpetrators have never been brought to justice, forced him to spend years in exile. He returned to contest the 2020 presidential election against the late President John Magufuli, but lost in a vote that the opposition alleged was marred by widespread irregularities. Lissu subsequently returned to exile before coming back to Tanzania in 2023, following President Samia's decision to lift a ban on opposition political rallies. His return was initially seen as a sign of renewed political openness after years of restrictions under Magufuli, who died in office in 2021. But relations between the government and the opposition deteriorated as the country approached the 2025 election. Lissu became Chadema's national chairman in January 2025 and intensified his demands for electoral reforms. His conviction is likely to deepen concerns about the state of democracy in Tanzania. Last week, Amnesty accused the government of continuing its crackdown following the election and "weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear". The authorities did not respond to a request for comment. Correction: An initial version of this story said Lissu had been convicted of inciting treason. We have corrected this to incitement. A panel of three judges at the High Court in Dar es Salaam acquitted him of the more serious offence of treason, saying prosecutors had failed to prove a key element of that charge. But they said the 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, had encouraged his supporters to disrupt the disputed 2025 general election. Lissu, who leads the opposition Chadema party, has denied the charges, describing the prosecution as politically motivated. The court said his campaign slogan "No Reforms, No Election" was sufficient for him to be convicted of the charge of incitement. "By uttering those words with the intention of disseminating them to the public, the accused incited the public to disrupt the 2025 elections," the court ruled. Lissu said he had only been charged with treason, not incitement. "The offence of incitement is one that you, honourable judges, have manufactured. You have created an offence that did not exist, and you have done so on political directives," Lissu told the court. He added that he would like to apply for bail as this was possible for incitement, unlike treason. He has leave to appeal at the Court of Appeal - the country's highest court. But if the four-year sentence is upheld, it would rule him out of the next elections, due in 2030. Treason is among Tanzania's most serious offences and can carry the death penalty. Human rights group Amnesty International described his conviction as a "travesty of justice". "Tundu Lissu should never have been arrested, let alone prosecuted and convicted," said its regional director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah: President Samia Suluhu Hassan won the October 2025 election with 98% of the vote - a result the opposition dismissed the result as a "mockery" of democracy as her two main challengers, including Lissu, were excluded. Her government has repeatedly denied targeting its opponents. The Chadema leader was arrested six months before the poll, shortly after launching a campaign demanding changes to the electoral system under the slogan "No Reforms, No Election". Prosecutors accused him of making statements intended to incite the public to disrupt the election and threaten the government. They argued that his remarks, which were also circulated online, amounted to treason. But Lissu, a lawyer who represented himself during the trial, maintained that his comments were part of a legitimate political campaign for constitutional and electoral reform. He argued that prosecutors had taken his statements out of context and failed to prove that he had committed any crime. Some of the demands raised by Chadema were: - Electoral commissioners should be independently appointed (not by the president) - Police should allow all parties to campaign free of intimidation - Government-appointed district chiefs should no longer act as returning officers - Party agents should be able to observe counting without harassment - It should be possible to challenge presidential election results in court. During his time in remand custody at Dar es Salaam's Ukonga Prison, Lissu went on hunger strike twice for brief periods when he said he was not allowed access to his lawyers or relatives. He also complained that guards listened to what should have been private consultations his lawyers. These allegations have been denied by the prison authorities. His case has attracted international attention, with rights groups expressing concern about the treatment of opposition politicians and the shrinking space for political dissent in Tanzania. Last year's election was followed by widespread protests and a violent security crackdown that left at least 500 people dead, according to an official inquiry. Opposition groups have said the death toll was much higher and demanded an independent investigation. The government has defended its handling of the unrest and rejected accusations of widespread political repression. Samia, 66, has insisted the election was fair and transparent and blamed foreigners for the unrest, saying it was part of a plot to overthrow her. She has set up another commission to inquiry to identify those behind the violence. Lissu has long been one of Tanzania's most outspoken critics of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM) party, which, along with its predecessor Tanu, has dominated the country's politics since independence. He first became an MP in 2010, representing a constituency near his birth place in Singida, 320km (200 miles) north-west of the capital, Dodoma. In September 2017, the Chadema politician narrowly survived an assassination attempt when gunmen sprayed his vehicle with bullets outside his home in Dodoma. He was shot multiple times and underwent extensive medical treatment abroad. The attack, whose perpetrators have never been brought to justice, forced him to spend years in exile. He returned to contest the 2020 presidential election against the late President John Magufuli, but lost in a vote that the opposition alleged was marred by widespread irregularities. Lissu subsequently returned to exile before coming back to Tanzania in 2023, following President Samia's decision to lift a ban on opposition political rallies. His return was initially seen as a sign of renewed political openness after years of restrictions under Magufuli, who died in office in 2021. But relations between the government and the opposition deteriorated as the country approached the 2025 election. Lissu became Chadema's national chairman in January 2025 and intensified his demands for electoral reforms. His conviction is likely to deepen concerns about the state of democracy in Tanzania. Last week, Amnesty accused the government of continuing its crackdown following the election and "weaponising counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear". The authorities did not respond to a request for comment. Correction: An initial version of this story said Lissu had been convicted of inciting treason. We have corrected this to incitement. news.titleTr: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
news.summaryTr: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".
news.articleText: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people - Published A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children. Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus". Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity. "The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law," the judge added. The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast. The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention. The court sentenced Mackenzie to 100 years in prison for homicide and another 100 years for offences related to starvation. The sentences within each category will run concurrently, but the two sets will run consecutively, bringing his total prison term to 200 years. Mackenzie also faces separate manslaughter and terrorism charges, which he denies. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that the scale and circumstances of the killings warranted the harshest punishment. However, Justice Mochache declined to impose the death penalty, despite ruling that the case met the threshold for its consideration. "Nevertheless, the court declines the invitation to impose the death penalty on any of the victims," she said, adding that capital punishment would eliminate any prospect of rehabilitation and disengagement. The death sentence has not been carried out in Kenya since 1987. Mackenzie was tried alongside 28 accomplices, including guards who enforced his fasting orders and gravediggers who helped conceal the victims' bodies in mass graves. They received varying prison sentences of up to 160 years. Justice Mochache described the killings as "cold and calculated", saying the perpetrators had shown no remorse and had even declared their willingness to fast to death themselves. Before the hearing began on Friday morning, Francis Wanje, who lost eight relatives including two grandchildren in Shakahola forest, told the BBC's Newsday programme that he was "hoping for... a sentence which will match his [Mackenzie's] deeds in the forest". Mackenzie and the co-accused had asked for leniency from the court. Before their conviction on 19 October, they had all pleaded not guilty and repeatedly insisted that nobody was forced to die. Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece", Justice Mochache said as she delivered her eight-hour judgement last month. Those who opposed Mackenzie's teachings were beaten to death. One of his co-accused said he had told his followers that anyone who "resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows". Burials inside the forest where the cult was based were called "weddings" and those who died "were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus" the judge said. The judge found that the deaths arose from an organised system, including religious teachings and directives that compelled followers to follow the deadly fasting. Post-mortem results showed the cause of deaths to be starvation for most victims, while others died from suffocation, strangulation or head injuries. The cause of death could not be determined for some, with their bodies having decomposed, while others died soon after their rescue as they were so emaciated. The Shakahola deaths have shone a spotlight on the lack of oversight of rogue religious activities and how they could have carried on for so long. The gravity of the case prompted President William Ruto to set up a commission of inquiry, although this was later declared unconstitutional. Investigations by the state-funded Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) revealed that local administration and law enforcement officials had repeatedly turned a blind eye to the cult's activities. "We expected at that time the police would take action immediately to go and rescue the other members there, but it didn't happen," said Wanje, who reported the case to the police in March 2023. Wanje said a relative of his in the police force and a former cult participant had managed to save his grandson at the time. The child told the police what had happened and showed them the grave of his siblings. "It was [supposed to be] his last day.. they [would have killed] my grandson." The cult leader had previously been arrested and later released for lack of evidence. Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003. Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity, drawing thousands of followers in its branches across Kenya. The church ran a television station called Times TV which would broadcast his sermons from his church in Malindi. His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil". The main church shut down in 2019 and Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him. While the conclusion of the murder cases may bring a sense of justice for the victims and their families, the convictions only account for 191 victims, while more than 400 bodies were exhumed from the forest. news.titleTr: What Democrats’ US midterm sweep means for the CLARITY Act
news.summaryTr: The CLARITY Act faces a new test as Democrats control Congress, raising questions over consumer protections, ethics and what the crypto industry may have to concede.
news.articleText: What Democrats’ US midterm sweep means for the CLARITY Act The CLARITY Act faces a new test as Democrats control Congress, raising questions over consumer protections, ethics and what the crypto industry may have to concede. Crypto companies contributed $233 million to political committees during the 2026 US midterm cycle, according to Public Citizen’s analysis of federal filings. Democrats won both chambers of Congress and will take control in January, giving them a chance to reshape the stalled CLARITY Act, a bill to set federal rules for crypto markets. In Ohio, Democrat and longtime crypto skeptic Sherrod Brown defeated Republican Sen. Jon Husted despite crypto-backed political action committees spending $64 million to defeat him. Senator Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s most vocal critics in Washington and the most senior Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, is expected to chair the panel in the next Congress. Stronger consumer protections, tougher scrutiny of political conflicts and a shift in regulatory power are all likely to be on the docket in the next round of negotiations. But a Democratic majority doesn’t have to kill the prospect of crypto market structure legislation completely. Democrat Congressman Shri Thanedar remains hopeful that the CLARITY Act can still pass, but says any legislation must include stronger ethics requirements. He tells Magazine: “President Trump’s blatant corruption has set back progress on crypto legislation, so Democrats will need strong anti-corruption provisions that apply to the President, not just Congress.” Can the industry’s political influence still be converted into legislation, and what will it have to concede to get there? A different deal for crypto The Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act in September, with disagreements over ethics provisions contributing to the impasse. The crypto spent $233 million on the 2026 US midterm elections. Source: Public Citizen Democrats are already reportedly discussing how to reshape the market structure debate, with House Democrats said to be considering expanding proposals from Representative Maxine Waters into a broader market structure bill. Related: Trump’s memecoin ventures derailed CLARITY Act, Scaramucci says That bill could include stronger consumer protections, a greater role for the Securities and Exchange Commission, and new ethics restrictions on public officials’ crypto activities. That could finally mean separating the industry’s push for clearer rules from the controversies surrounding Trump’s personal crypto ventures. Democrats have already signaled plans to investigate the Trump family’s business dealings and other corporate interests, with incoming House Oversight Committee Chair Robert Garcia planning to pursue inquiries into corporate corruption. Hadley Stern, head of institutions at Silence Laboratories and founder of Fidelity Digital Assets, says Democrats are right to “go after” the second, and the industry should want them to; that’s “what’s poisoning the bipartisan deal,” he says. “A sitting president’s family launching memecoins and a stablecoin is a real governance problem,” he tells Magazine. “If I’d done that at Fidelity, I’d have been walked out the same afternoon.” He says 2026’s digital asset industry is very different from the last time Democrats “held the gavel,” pointing to its growth from “FTX and a bunch of tokens” in 2022 to a federal law for stablecoins, Treasuries and credit funds onchain and tokenized equities on the way: “You don’t regulate that by pretending it doesn’t exist.” What would the industry have to concede? The industry may also have to accept more demanding standards if it wants legislation that can survive changes in political control. Paul Brody, founder and CEO of Nightfall Networks and former global blockchain lead at EY, expects banks “to come out winners,” as they will “push for crypto companies” to be held to the same exacting consumer protection and security standards. Related: Crypto Biz: CLARITY Act setback puts Coinbase in the spotlight He says the industry has opposed this, but tells Magazine that “a wise strategy” would be to “accept similar conditions,” given that blockchain-native ecosystems are still “vastly more flexible, programmable and efficient.” Lindsay Fraser, chief policy officer at Blockchain Association, also argues consumer protection and innovation should not be treated as competing objectives. “We can protect consumers while ensuring the law reflects how the technology actually works,” she says, adding the goal is “lasting policy that earns public trust, gives builders a future in this country, and strengthens American financial leadership.” That doesn’t mean it’s all smooth sailing to a potential compromise. Brody says there’s still the possibility of a presidential veto, and points out that crypto is likely to be a “low priority” compared to “investigations of corruption and battles over budgets and the war.” How the Binance hack could influence lawmakers The midterm results came as lawmakers were already grappling with the fallout from the Binance hack, the largest hack in crypto history, with over $6.3 billion stolen on Oct. 29, raising fresh concerns about exchange security and customer protections. Thanedar says while the legislation “wouldn’t solve every potential problem,” it would provide “much-needed certainty” and “security guardrails,” and the hack provides a “clear example of the danger of not enacting appropriate legislation.” Maylea Ma, deputy general counsel at 1inch, says rather than making a stronger case for passing the latest draft of CLARITY, the incident “highlights problems the legislation does not address.” The hack involved a “centralized exchange’s hot wallet and signing failure,” Ma says, but the current draft “has no insurer, no loss payee, and no hot wallet cap that would have mitigated the loss for Binance or imposed security standards that would have prevented the hack.” Amanda Fischer, policy director at Better Markets, said the episode highlighted how “unfit for purpose the crypto ecosystem is for mainstream finance,” and crypto exchanges should not act as custodians, since it creates a “honeypot risk.” Binance hack shows how ‘unfit’ crypto is for mainstream finance. Source: Amanda Fischer Ma says the incident is “likely to impact” the next vote on CLARITY and could make lawmakers less willing to pass legislation the industry wants, unless it comes with stronger consumer protections. Crypto spent years convincing Washington it deserves a seat at the table; now it will need to agree on the obligations that come along with it. Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust, 13 kat getiri sağladığı Tesla'daki tüm hisselerini satarken SpaceX'teki payını da azalttı. Elon Musk'ın şirketlerinin ilk büyük yatırımcılarından Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust, portföyünde önemli değişikliklere gitti. Baillie Gifford tarafından yönetilen ve Londra Borsası'nda işlem gören yatırım fonu, Tesla'daki hisselerinin tamamını elden çıkarırken SpaceX'teki pozisyonunu da önemli ölçüde küçülttü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Fonun cuma günü açıkladığı altı aylık finansal sonuçlara göre, SpaceX'in toplam varlıklar içindeki payı 30 Eylül'deki yüzde 15 seviyesinden 4 Kasım itibarıyla yüzde 11,1'e geriledi. Scottish Mortgage, Tesla'daki kalan hisselerini ise nisan ayında satarak 2013'te başlayan yatırımını tamamen sonlandırdı. Tesla yatırımından 13 kat getiri sağladı Scottish Mortgage, Tesla'ya ilk yatırımını 2013 yılında gerçekleştirdi. Fon, yaklaşık 13 yıl boyunca sürdürdüğü yatırımından önemli kazanç elde etti. Temmuz ayında açıklanan verilere göre Tesla'ya yaklaşık 470 milyon dolar yatıran fon, bu süreçte yaklaşık 6,2 milyar dolar gerçekleşmiş kâr sağladı. Şirket, yatırımının başlangıç sermayesinin 13 katına ulaşan getiri sunduğunu bildirdi. Fon yönetimi, Tesla'dan çıkış kararında şirketin otonom sürüş ve robotik alanlarındaki büyüme potansiyelinin hisse fiyatına büyük ölçüde yansımış olmasının etkili olduğunu belirtti. Ayrıca Tesla'nın temel otomotiv faaliyetlerinde, özellikle Çin pazarında artan rekabetin de yatırım kararında rol oynadığı ifade edildi. SpaceX'teki payını azalttı Scottish Mortgage'ın SpaceX yatırımı da fonun en başarılı işlemleri arasında yer aldı. Fon, Elon Musk'ın uzay şirketine ilk yatırımını Aralık 2018'de, SpaceX'in yaklaşık 31 milyar dolar değerlemeye sahip olduğu dönemde yaptı. 2021 yılına kadar şirkete yaklaşık 200 milyon dolarlık yatırım taahhüdünde bulundu. SpaceX'in roket fırlatma faaliyetlerini genişletmesi ve Starlink uydu internet ağını büyütmesiyle yatırımın değeri hızla arttı. Haziran 2026'da gerçekleştirilen halka arz sırasında SpaceX, Scottish Mortgage'ın portföy değerinin yaklaşık dörtte birini oluşturuyordu. Halka arz sonrasında hisse satış kısıtlamalarının aşamalı olarak kaldırılmasıyla fon, SpaceX hisselerinin bir bölümünü sattı. Scottish Mortgage yönetimi, buna rağmen SpaceX'in uzun vadeli büyüme potansiyeline yönelik olumlu görüşünü koruduğunu vurguladı. Fon, pozisyonun azaltılmasını portföy yönetiminde risklerin dengelenmesine yönelik bir adım olarak değerlendirdi. Fonun altı aylık getirisi yüzde 31,5 oldu SpaceX yatırımı, Scottish Mortgage'ın finansal performansına da önemli katkı sağladı. Fonun 30 Eylül'de sona eren altı aylık dönemde net varlık değeri bazındaki toplam getirisi yüzde 31,5'e ulaştı. Aynı dönemde FTSE All-World Endeksi yüzde 16 getiri sağlarken fonun hisse fiyatındaki yükseliş yüzde 33,8 oldu. SpaceX yatırımı tek başına fonun toplam getirisine yaklaşık 8 puan katkıda bulundu. Şirket ayrıca SpaceX hisselerinin satışından elde edilen gelirin borçların geri ödenmesinde kullanıldığını ve böylece kaldıraç oranının düşürüldüğünü açıkladı. Musk'ın şirketlerinde 420 milyar dolarlık değer kaybı Fonun portföy değişiklikleri, Elon Musk'ın şirketlerinin piyasalarda sert satış baskısıyla karşılaştığı bir döneme denk geldi. ABD ara seçimlerinin ardından artan siyasi ve düzenleyici risk endişeleriyle SpaceX hisseleri perşembe günü yaklaşık yüzde 9, Tesla hisseleri ise yüzde 11 değer kaybetti. İki şirketin toplam piyasa değerindeki azalma, salı günkü kapanışa kıyasla 420 milyar doları aştı. Yatırımcıların, ABD Kongresi'nde Musk'ın şirketlerine yönelik yeni soruşturmalar başlatılabileceği ve daha sıkı düzenlemelerin gündeme gelebileceği ihtimalini fiyatladığı belirtildi.

news.title: Nigeria sets new crypto licensing rules, bans algorithmic stablecoins
news.summary: Nigeria has banned algorithmic stablecoins and introduced reserve requirements for issuers as it expands central bank oversight of crypto payment services.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Nigeria sets new crypto licensing rules, bans algorithmic stablecoins
news.summaryTr: Nigeria has banned algorithmic stablecoins and introduced reserve requirements for issuers as it expands central bank oversight of crypto payment services.
news.articleText: Nigeria sets new crypto licensing rules, bans algorithmic stablecoins Nigeria has banned algorithmic stablecoins and introduced reserve requirements for issuers as it expands central bank oversight of crypto payment services. Nigeria’s central bank has introduced new licensing and reserve requirements for cryptocurrency companies, tightening oversight of stablecoins and digital asset payment services in one of Africa’s largest crypto markets. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) issued the Regulations for the Operations of Non-Security Virtual Assets on Thursday, establishing rules for stablecoin issuers, crypto payment providers, exchanges, custodians and other covered service providers. The regulations took effect immediately, though existing operators have 180 days to apply for licenses or authorizations. The CBN said the framework aims to support responsible innovation while protecting consumers and financial stability. The move follows President Bola Tinubu’s July executive order, which sought to coordinate crypto oversight among Nigerian authorities without changing their existing powers. Stablecoin issuers face new capital and reserve rules Under the new regulations, stablecoin issuers must fully back their tokens with reserve assets and maintain an additional buffer equal to at least 2% of their value. At least 40% of reserves must consist of cash or qualifying highly liquid assets. The rules also set minimum paid-up capital of 10 billion naira ($7.4 million) for naira-backed issuers and 15 billion naira ($11.1 million) for foreign currency-backed stablecoin issuers. Additionally, companies providing payment-related crypto services, including exchange and custody services, must maintain minimum paid-up capital of 1 billion naira ($742,000). The regulations also prohibit stablecoins that rely primarily on algorithms rather than eligible reserves to maintain their value, along with tokens that lack enforceable redemption rights. Nigeria’s crypto crackdown enters a new phase Nigeria has taken a restrictive approach to crypto trading, previously limiting banking access for exchanges and seeking to restrict peer-to-peer trading using local currency. The country drew international attention in the crypto industry over its dispute with Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume. Binance discontinued its Nigerian naira services in March 2024 amid government scrutiny of crypto trading and allegations of currency manipulation. Nigerian authorities also detained Binance executive Tigran Gambaryan for nearly eight months before dropping money laundering charges against him in October 2024. More recently, Nigeria’s revenue agency introduced crypto tax collection rules for digital asset platforms and peer-to-peer marketplaces in August 2026. news.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

news.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
news.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Binance’s $6.3 billion security incident has left unanswered questions about how the exchange managed its hot wallets and limited the amount attackers could access, exchanges moved to reassure customers about their cold storage reserves following Binance’s hack, and Bitcoin plunged below $76,000 as US stocks erased gains made after the midterm elections. Binance’s $6.3B hack leaves questions over hot wallet safeguards Binance’s $6.3 billion security incident has left unanswered questions about how the exchange managed its hot wallets and limited the amount attackers could access. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on Oct. 30 that the attack affected the exchange’s own hot wallet. Most customer assets were held in offline cold storage and moved to hot wallets only when users requested withdrawals. Wallet balances offer only a partial picture of an exchange’s exposure to an attack. Public blockchain records can show funds moving but cannot establish the internal controls governing those transfers, CertiK analyst Jonathan Riss told Cointelegraph. In its initial report Tuesday, Binance said attackers accessed an internal wallet-signing service to move funds outside its normal withdrawal process. Binance said some technical details would remain confidential to prevent further attacks. Crypto exchanges tout cold storage ratios after Binance attack Crypto exchanges were quick to reassure users following the attack on Binance’s hot wallet infrastructure last week, with several companies disclosing how they divide assets between cold storage and internet-connected hot wallets this week. Crypto exchange Gate on Thursday launched a “Proof of Security” (PoSEC) framework, reporting that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage and 11.74% in hot wallets. It claims its cold storage could cover 104.58% of customer assets even if its hot wallets were completely drained. “By publicly disclosing the distribution of assets between platform cold storage and hot wallets, PoSEC provides visibility into asset storage structures and their ability to cover potential losses under extreme scenarios,” Gate said. It noted the data is still undergoing independent review by a third-party audit firm. Threat actors attacked Binance’s hot-wallet infrastructure last week, stealing approximately $6.36 billion, most of it in about 20 minutes, according to TRM Labs. Binance CEO Richard Teng said the “vast majority” of user assets are held in cold wallets, but the company has not provided a precise split. Bitcoin crashes 6% to 7-week low as US stocks erase election gains Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $76,000 on Thursday as risk assets abruptly reversed their US midterm elections rally. After making swift gains on the back of a Democrat sweep of the US House of Representatives and Senate, equities saw sharp selling on Thursday as traders rotated out of tech. Crypto markets liquidated nearly $500 million in positioning in the first hour of the US trading session, per data from CoinGlass, with 24-hour total liquidations nearing $850 million. Now targeting $76,000, BTC/USD approached the bottom of its one-month trading range. The pair risked losing support at the 50-week simple moving average (SMA), currently at $75,733. In his latest analysis, crypto trader Rekt Capital noted that Bitcoin was repeating behavior from May, when a period of rangebound moves around $80,000 subsequently gave way to a breakdown and new macro lows of $57,000 in late June.

news.title: Ethereum devs won’t fork Glamsterdam on Hoodi until smart contract risks resolved
news.summary: Ethereum developers are investigating concerns tied to eight smart contract invariants tied to Glamsterdam’s EIP-8037 and EIP-8038.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Ethereum devs won’t fork Glamsterdam on Hoodi until smart contract risks resolved
news.summaryTr: Ethereum developers are investigating concerns tied to eight smart contract invariants tied to Glamsterdam’s EIP-8037 and EIP-8038.
news.articleText: Ethereum devs won’t fork Glamsterdam on Hoodi until smart contract risks resolved Ethereum developers are investigating concerns tied to eight smart contract invariants tied to Glamsterdam’s EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. Ethereum core developers delayed the Glamsterdam upgrade’s implementation on the Hoodi testnet until security concerns tied to eight smart contract invariants are resolved. Some existing Ethereum projects rely on assumptions that certain operations would cost a specific amount of gas, which would be invalidated by Glamsterdam’s EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 because they change how gas is charged for certain operations, the Ethereum Foundation said in a Friday blog post. The decision followed an Oct. 13 report from smart contract auditor ChainSecurity, which found that the two Ethereum Improvement Proposals (EIPs) could break smart contracts that rely on fixed gas-related assumptions when external calls fail. Delaying the Hoodi testnet fork gives developers more time to identify potential smart contract issues and determine whether changes are needed before Glamsterdam progresses toward mainnet deployment. The Hoodi fork will not proceed until the issues are resolved, added the Ethereum Foundation’s post. Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade went live on the Sepolia testnet on Oct. 6, in one of its final major rehearsals. The upgrade aims to advance Ethereum’s layer-1 scaling roadmap with enshrined proposer-builder separation, block-level access lists and changes to gas pricing that better reflect the cost of execution, the Ethereum Foundation announced in a Sept. 28 blog post. news.titleTr: Solana’s Shanghai event halted over unauthorized promotion: Report
news.summaryTr: Solana’s promotional campaigns through domestic entities allegedly violated China’s crypto-related restrictions, an unidentified PBOC official told China’s Financial News.
news.articleText: Solana’s Shanghai event halted over unauthorized promotion: Report Solana’s promotional campaigns through domestic entities allegedly violated China’s crypto-related restrictions, an unidentified PBOC official told China’s Financial News. Chinese authorities halted the Solana Accelerate event in Shanghai over alleged unauthorized promotional activities involving domestic entities, China’s state-backed Financial News reported on Friday. The outlet cited an unidentified official from a department of the People’s Bank of China (PBOC), who said Solana had promoted its brand through domestic entities, including by placing advertisements on a building in Shanghai’s Lujiazui financial district. The official also claimed that Solana provides technical services supporting the issuance and trading of cryptocurrencies, which he described as illegal financial activities under Chinese regulations. It marked the second reported disruption of a Solana event in mainland China in the past two years, highlighting how the country’s restrictions extend beyond digital asset trading. An October 2025 Solana event in Shenzhen was also cut short over venue capacity and public-safety concerns, according to an X announcement by Solana’s Chinese-speaking community. In an Oct. 16 X post, Solana Foundation president Lily Liu said organizers postponed the Shanghai event to “comply with local requirements” after an event registration unexpectedly quadrupled, exceeding the event cap pre-registered with local authorities. In a February notice, the PBOC and several other agencies doubled down on crypto-related restrictions and included a new ban on the unauthorized issuance of yuan-pegged stablecoins. news.summary: The cybersecurity company flagged similar multi-stage intrusion patterns behind other high-profile crypto heists, including the $388 million Bitget hack.

news.titleTr: Binance hackers had 8 weeks of access before $6.3B exploit, Security Alliance estimates
news.summaryTr: The cybersecurity company flagged similar multi-stage intrusion patterns behind other high-profile crypto heists, including the $388 million Bitget hack.
news.articleText: Binance hackers had 8 weeks of access before $6.3B exploit, Security Alliance estimates The cybersecurity company flagged similar multi-stage intrusion patterns behind other high-profile crypto heists, including the $388 million Bitget hack. Non-profit cybersecurity organization Security Alliance (SEAL) estimates that the North Korea-linked TraderTraitor gained access to Binance’s systems about eight weeks before the $6.3 billion exploit on Oct. 29. The hacking group gained access to Binance’s systems sometime in September, wrote SEAL in a Thursday report, adding that threat actors can navigate these systems with a “high degree of stealth over prolonged periods of time” after initial intrusion. SEAL identified at least four “front companies” associated with TraderTraitor’s fake recruitment campaigns in 2026, including citalab.net, citalab.com, bitfit.io and oddium.io. The cybersecurity organization’s analysis pointed to similar multi-stage intrusion patterns in other high-profile crypto hacks. It estimated that attackers had about six weeks of access before the $388 million Bitget hack, six weeks of access to LayerZero before the vulnerability that led to the $293 million Kelp DAO exploit and about three weeks before conducting the $24 million AFX exploit. Cointelegraph contacted Binance for comment on the estimates but did not receive a response by publication. Binance attributed the $6.3 billion hack to a fake job interview that enabled hackers to compromise an employee device and steal credentials to breach the exchange’s wallet infrastructure. Binance traced the attack campaign back to June, when a separate employee’s device was compromised. The exchange detected the incident and replaced the device, but said that attackers had already gathered information about its team and wallet infrastructure, according to a Tuesday X post. The US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor, in a Saturday report. Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, dismissed the accusations. Related: Binance hack may be ‘temporary setback’ for crypto, Grayscale’s Pandl says

news.title: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia
news.summary: The scandal involves senior members of President Prabowo Subianto's government, and hint at growing tensions among its elites.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia
news.summaryTr: The scandal involves senior members of President Prabowo Subianto's government, and hint at growing tensions among its elites.
news.articleText: What to know about the presidential wiretapping scandal rocking Indonesia - Published Authorities are investigating possible treason in Indonesia after a bombshell announcement this week that President Prabowo Subianto's phone conversations might have been spied on. Several senior figures of Prabowo's administration have been embroiled in the wiretapping scandal, including his chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - who is not related to the president despite his name. It is unfolding against what many have interpreted as a widening rift between Prabowo and his predecessor, Joko Widodo - otherwise know as Jokowi - who had thrown his support behind Prabowo's 2024 presidential campaign. "Listyo's position, as we know, is actually very close to Jokowi," Made Supriatma, a visiting fellow at Singapore's ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute, told BBC Indonesian. "So now it's practically said that they're going their separate ways." What happened? Listyo Sigit Prabowo, the president's chief of staff, was arrested on Tuesday along with two senior police officers for allegedly wiretapping President Prabowo. The three men are suspected of keying phone numbers, including Prabowo's, into the police's official electronic surveillance system - which allows authorities to intercept communications - without following proper procedures, such as obtaining an investigation warrant or case report. Authorities say the operation was discovered last week after a tip-off from a police officer. But they believe the alleged wiretapping stretches back to 2025, when Listyo was serving as the national police chief. This could amount to treason, as it involved "sensitive information" that could "endanger the interests and sovereignty of the nation", a spokesperson for the president told reporters on Wednesday. In Indonesia, treason is punishable by life imprisonment or even the death penalty - though the country has not executed anyone in a decade. The spokesperson said the motive behind the alleged wiretapping remained unclear. It was not just President Prabowo who was targeted in the alleged wiretapping operation, either. Other targets included politicians, journalists, NGO representatives and businesspeople, authorities said. On Thursday evening, police named a fourth suspect: Slamet Uliandi, from the national police criminal investigation unit. But he was not detained due to his ill health after suffering a stroke, according to authorities. Listyo, who was appointed the president's chief of staff last month, was sacked from his new position shortly after his arrest. This is not the first wiretapping scandal to have involved Indonesia's leaders. In 2014, several wiretapping devices were discovered at Jokowi's official residence when he was the governor of Jakarta. Former president Megawati Soekarnoputri claimed in 2024 that she had avoided using her personal mobile phone number because she was the target of wiretapping. Indonesia's police chief Suyudi Ario Seto told reporters on Thursday that the probe into wiretapping was "purely law enforcement and has nothing to do with rivalries or anything else". But many see it as the latest blow in a disintegrating alliance between President Prabowo and former president Jokowi, who led the country from 2014 to 2024. Prabowo vs Jokowi Jokowi had thrown his support behind Prabowo in the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, as part of an alliance that ultimately propelled Prabowo to become Indonesia's next leader. Riding to victory with him was Gibran Rakabuming Raka, Jokowi's eldest son, who became Indonesia's vice president. Two years on, that alliance appears to be fracturing - even if neither party has confirmed the rift. Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country. In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many of Jokowi's allies into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati. Meanwhile, uncertainty also looms over Gibran, Jokowi's son, who is mired in a growing controversy over the validity of his high school credentials, a pre-requisite to run for vice presidency. He now faces calls to be disqualified from his job, on the grounds that he should not have been eligible as a candidate. The wiretapping scandal and subsequent arrest of Listyo - who rose to the top of the police force in Jokowi's administration, and is seen as one of the ex-president's longtime allies - is now adding to the tensions between Prabowo and Jokowi. When asked about the wiretapping incident after the court session on Thursday, Jokowi told reporters that "we should all respect the ongoing legal process". This latest scandal comes during a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. His flagship free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation. Experts, meanwhile, say all this has distracted from the more pressing challenges that Indonesians are facing on the ground - from economic uncertainties to environmental pollution. In recent months, protesters have taken to the streets to pressure the government on a range of issues such as toxic wildfire haze, corruption, and cost-of-living woes. "It's like we're living in a country on autopilot," Nicky Fahrizal, a researcher at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies in Indonesia, told BBC Indonesian. "Because the way the government operates proves that it's not the people's interests that are being pursued, but rather the interests of individual groups."

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.titleTr: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
news.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-
news.articleTextTr: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction
news.articleText: Release Number 9315-26 CFTC Sues to Block State Enforcement in Utah Amid Ongoing Efforts to Preserve Jurisdiction October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced today it has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws. The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law. “Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.” This action reflects the CFTC’s firm commitment to maintaining its exclusive jurisdiction over CFTC-registered prediction markets. The CFTC continues to draw a clear line: if a state challenges the lawful operation of a derivatives exchange, the Commission will protect federal sovereign interests. The Commission has also initiated legal proceedings against nine other states and has submitted briefs in four federal courts of appeal and one state supreme court. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Enka İnşaat'ın (ENKAI) kârı yüzde 17 geriledi! 3. çeyrek bilançosu beklenti altında kaldı - Enka İnşaat, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 3,42 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Şirketin 9 aylık net kârı yıllık yüzde 17 düşüşle 21,87 milyar TL'ye gerilerken, çeyreklik sonuçlar piyasa beklentisini karşılayamadı. Enka İnşaat ve Sanayi A.Ş. (ENKAI), 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğine ilişkin finansal sonuçlarını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. Şirket, temmuz-eylül döneminde 3 milyar 422 milyon 270 bin TL net kâr elde etti. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Böylece Enka'nın 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayındaki toplam net kârı 21 milyar 869 milyon 395 bin TL oldu. Şirketin geçen yılın aynı döneminde açıkladığı 26,28 milyar TL'lik net kârla karşılaştırıldığında, yıllık bazda yüzde 17 düşüş kaydedildi. Kâr beklentilerin altında kaldı Matriks Haber tarafından gerçekleştirilen bilanço anketine 8 aracı kurum katıldı. Ankete göre Enka İnşaat için üçüncü çeyrek ortalama net kâr beklentisi 5 milyar 129 milyon TL, medyan beklenti ise 4 milyar 944 milyon 200 bin TL seviyesindeydi. Şirketin açıkladığı 3,42 milyar TL'lik net kâr, hem ortalama hem de medyan beklentinin altında gerçekleşti. Böylece Enka, üçüncü çeyrek bilançosunda piyasa tahminlerini karşılayamadı. Satışlar yüzde 20 artarken faaliyet kârı geriledi Enka İnşaat'ın 2026 yılının ilk dokuz ayında elde ettiği hasılat, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 108,97 milyar TL'den 130,22 milyar TL'ye yükseldi. Böylece satış gelirleri yıllık yüzde 20 artış gösterdi. Buna karşın esas faaliyet kârı 20,66 milyar TL'den 18,24 milyar TL'ye gerileyerek yüzde 12 düşüş kaydetti. FAVÖK de geçen yılki 23,99 milyar TL seviyesinden 23,80 milyar TL'ye indi. Varlıklar ve özkaynaklar yükseldi Enka'nın toplam varlıkları 2025 yıl sonundaki 493,06 milyar TL seviyesinden 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreği itibarıyla 565,13 milyar TL'ye çıktı. Aynı dönemde toplam borçlar 113,52 milyar TL'den 126,29 milyar TL'ye yükseldi. Şirketin özkaynakları ise 373,22 milyar TL'den 431,78 milyar TL'ye ulaştı. Özkaynaklarda çeyreklik dönemde yüzde 5 artış kaydedildi. Enka İnşaat'ın 2026 üçüncü çeyrek bilançosu Şirketin piyasa çarpanlarında F/K oranı 15,27, PD/DD oranı 1,12 olarak açıklandı. Enka İnşaat'ın piyasa değeri ise 485,10 milyar TL seviyesinde bulunuyor.
